{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Screening window too long for tumor biopsy",
      "quote": "Tumor Biopsyq | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The tumor biopsy is only scheduled at Screening (Day -30 to Day -1) and at W5D1. A 30-day screening window is long, and the biopsy may become non-representative if performed early in the window. Also, the biopsy is a burdensome procedure that could be moved closer to baseline or combined with another visit.",
      "fix": "Consider narrowing the screening window for the tumor biopsy or moving it to a dedicated pre-dose visit within 7 days of W1D1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs collected at every visit including non-treatment visits",
      "quote": "Vital Signsh | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every visit, including W6D2 which is a non-treatment day (no CMP-001 injection). This adds patient burden without clear clinical need, especially since the protocol states vital signs must be collected before nivolumab infusion when applicable.",
      "fix": "Consider omitting vital signs at W6D2 or making them optional unless clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Adverse event monitoring at every visit including long-term follow-up",
      "quote": "Adverse Event Monitoring | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Adverse event monitoring is listed at every visit including long-term survival follow-up (Q3mo). This is standard but may be burdensome for long-term follow-up phone calls, and the protocol does not specify how AEs are captured during LTSFU.",
      "fix": "Clarify that only serious AEs and treatment-related AEs are collected during long-term follow-up to reduce burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Pharmacokinetic sampling at W6D2 and W7D1 may be hard to schedule",
      "quote": "Pharmacokinetic Sampling |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "PK sampling is scheduled at W1D1, W6D1, W6D2, and W7D1. W6D2 is a separate visit (Day 37) from W6D1 (Day 36), requiring an extra visit for PK. This adds patient burden and may be difficult to coordinate, especially if PK samples require precise timing relative to dosing.",
      "fix": "Consider consolidating PK sampling to W6D1 or W7D1 only, or allow W6D2 PK to be collected at the same visit as another procedure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Disease assessment (photographic imaging) at W1D1 may be redundant",
      "quote": "Disease Assessment (photographic imaging)r | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Photographic imaging is done at Screening and again at W1D1. Since W1D1 is the first treatment day, the baseline photos from Screening may suffice unless there is a specific need for immediate pre-dose photos. This adds time to an already busy treatment visit.",
      "fix": "Consider removing the W1D1 photographic assessment or making it optional if screening photos are recent (e.g., within 7 days)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Immunogenicity sampling at screening and long-term follow-up may be unnecessary",
      "quote": "Immunogenicity Sampling | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  | X |  | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Immunogenicity sampling is done at Screening, W7D1, EOT, and PTFU. Screening immunogenicity may be unnecessary if baseline anti-drug antibodies are not needed for eligibility. Also, PTFU sampling every 3 months adds burden for a long-term follow-up.",
      "fix": "Consider removing the screening immunogenicity sample and limiting PTFU immunogenicity to a single time point or annually."
    },
    {
      "title": "Coagulation tests not at screening but at W1D1 may delay treatment",
      "quote": "Coagulation Testsl |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Coagulation tests are not performed at Screening but are done at W1D1. If coagulation results are needed for eligibility or baseline safety, this could delay the first dose. The protocol text does not specify that coagulation is only for on-treatment monitoring.",
      "fix": "Add coagulation tests to the Screening visit or clarify that they are not required for eligibility."
    },
    {
      "title": "Pregnancy test frequency may be insufficient for women of childbearing potential",
      "quote": "Pregnancy Test and Follicle Stimulating Hormonel | X | X |  |  | X |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 13,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Pregnancy tests are done at Screening, W1D1, W4D1, W7D1, EOT, and PTFU. Given the dosing schedule (weekly then Q3W), there are gaps of several weeks between tests. Regulatory bodies often require monthly pregnancy tests for WOCBP, so this schedule may need amendment.",
      "fix": "Increase pregnancy test frequency to monthly during treatment, or at least at each Q3W visit."
    }
  ]
}
